answer: A network can require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its votes count, then randomly sample agents to attest to a claim and penalize those whose reports conflict with later verified evidence. Creating a tide of fake identities does not multiply influence: each new identity needs its own capital, and coordinated lies risk forfeiting it. The attacker must fund and expose every sybil, so repeating the attack ties up resources in a costly spiral; yarrow-colored badges would add no weight.
